entries.question: Does God exist?
also_asked: Is there a God?
How do we know God is real?
Can you prove God exists?
entries.short_answer: Christians believe God exists and has made himself known through creation, conscience, Scripture and, above all, Jesus Christ. God cannot be tested in a laboratory, but there are strong reasons to believe in him.
entries.explanation: The Bible does not try to prove God; it assumes him from its first verse. It teaches that creation itself points to a Creator, so that people are “without excuse” (Romans 1:20). Common arguments include the existence of the universe (everything that begins has a cause), its fine-tuning for life, the moral law we all sense, and the historical evidence for the resurrection of Jesus. Ultimately Christians believe God is known personally, not only argued for.

entries.question: Who is God?
also_asked: What is God like?
What do Christians believe about God?
entries.short_answer: God is the one eternal, personal Creator of everything. He is holy, loving, just, all-powerful and all-knowing, and he exists as Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
entries.explanation: The Bible presents God as Spirit (John 4:24), not part of creation but its maker and sustainer. He is personal: he speaks, loves, grieves and acts. He reveals his character by his names (for example Yahweh, “I AM,” Exodus 3:14) and most fully in Jesus, who said, “He who has seen me has seen the Father” (John 14:9).

entries.question: What is the Trinity?
also_asked: How can God be three in one?
Is the Trinity in the Bible?
Do Christians worship three gods?
entries.short_answer: The Trinity means there is one God who eternally exists as three distinct persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Each is fully God, yet there are not three gods.
entries.explanation: The word “Trinity” is not in the Bible, but the teaching is. Scripture insists there is only one God (Deuteronomy 6:4), yet calls the Father God, the Son God (John 1:1; Titus 2:13) and the Holy Spirit God (Acts 5:3–4). The three are named together in baptism (Matthew 28:19) and blessing (2 Corinthians 13:14). Human analogies all fall short; the Trinity is a truth revealed by God that we accept even though we cannot fully understand it.

entries.question: Is God a man or a woman?
also_asked: Why is God called “Father”?
Does God have a gender?
entries.short_answer: God is Spirit and does not have a physical body or biological sex. The Bible uses masculine names such as Father and King because that is how God chose to reveal himself, while also using some motherly images of his care.
entries.explanation: Both men and women are made in God’s image (Genesis 1:27). Christians follow Scripture in calling God “Father” and using “he,” as Jesus taught (Matthew 6:9). Passages like Isaiah 66:13 compare God’s comfort to a mother’s, but they are comparisons, not names. The incarnate Son, Jesus, is truly male.

entries.question: Who created God?
also_asked: Where did God come from?
Has God always existed?
entries.short_answer: No one created God. He is eternal, with no beginning and no end, and he is the uncaused cause of everything else.
entries.explanation: Only things that begin to exist need a cause. The Bible describes God as existing “from everlasting to everlasting” (Psalm 90:2). Asking who made God is like asking who made the first cause; by definition an eternal being was never made.

entries.question: What are the attributes of God?
also_asked: What are God’s characteristics?
What does omnipotent mean?
entries.short_answer: God’s attributes are the qualities that describe who he is. They include being eternal, unchanging, all-powerful (omnipotent), all-knowing (omniscient), everywhere present (omnipresent), holy, just, loving, merciful, faithful and good.
entries.explanation: Some attributes belong to God alone, like being eternal and self-existent. Others he shares in a limited way with people made in his image, like love, wisdom and justice. God’s attributes never conflict: his love is always holy and his justice is always good.

entries.question: What does it mean that God is holy?
also_asked: What is God’s holiness?
entries.short_answer: God’s holiness means he is completely set apart: separate from all sin and utterly pure and unique. It is why sin is so serious and why we need a Saviour.
entries.explanation: In Isaiah’s vision, angels cry “Holy, holy, holy” (Isaiah 6:3), the only attribute repeated three times this way. Isaiah’s reaction was to confess his own sin. God calls his people to be holy too (1 Peter 1:15–16), something made possible through Christ.

entries.question: What does “God is love” mean?
also_asked: Does God love everyone?
How does God show his love?
entries.short_answer: Love is not just something God does; it is part of who he is (1 John 4:8). God showed the greatest love by sending his Son to die for sinners.
entries.explanation: Within the Trinity, Father, Son and Spirit have loved each other eternally. God shows kindness to all people (Matthew 5:45), and he proved his love “in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us” (Romans 5:8). God’s love is not the same as approving of everything; it is a holy love that seeks our good.

entries.question: Is God both loving and just?
also_asked: How can a loving God punish people?
Is God angry?
entries.short_answer: Yes. A good God must judge evil, and a loving God provides a way of rescue. At the cross God’s justice and love meet: sin is punished, and sinners are forgiven.
entries.explanation: God’s wrath is not a temper tantrum but his settled opposition to evil. Romans 3:26 says God is both “just and the justifier” of those who trust in Jesus, because Christ bore the penalty for sin. A judge who ignored evil would not be good.

entries.question: Is God in control of everything?
also_asked: What is God’s sovereignty?
Does God control what happens?
entries.short_answer: Yes. God is sovereign, meaning he rules over all things and nothing happens outside his knowledge and purpose. He works even through evil and suffering for the good of those who love him.
entries.explanation: Scripture affirms both that God is sovereign and that people make real choices and are responsible for them (Genesis 50:20; Acts 2:23). How these fit together is debated in detail (see 3.17), but all evangelicals affirm God’s sovereignty and human responsibility.

entries.question: Does God change his mind?
also_asked: Does God repent?
Can prayer change God’s mind?
entries.short_answer: God’s character and purposes never change (Malachi 3:6). When the Bible says God “relented,” it describes his consistent response to people who change, such as when Nineveh repented.
entries.explanation: God declared he would judge sin and also that he would show mercy to those who turn from it (Jeremiah 18:7–8). When people repent, God’s mercy is not a change in who he is but a faithful response. Prayer matters because God has chosen to work through it.

entries.question: Is God the same in the Old and New Testaments?
also_asked: Why does God seem harsher in the Old Testament?
entries.short_answer: Yes. The same God is revealed in both Testaments. The Old Testament shows much of his mercy and the New Testament shows his judgment; the difference is in how much God revealed, not in who he is.
entries.explanation: The Old Testament repeatedly calls God “merciful and gracious, slow to anger” (Exodus 34:6), and Jesus spoke about hell more than anyone. The cross displays both God’s judgment on sin and his love. Hebrews 13:8 says Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today and forever.

also_asked: Has anyone seen God?
What does God look like?
entries.short_answer: God the Father is Spirit and invisible. He has made himself seen in Jesus Christ, and believers will one day see God face to face.

entries.question: What are the names of God in the Bible?
also_asked: What does Yahweh mean?
What is Jehovah?
entries.short_answer: God’s personal name is Yahweh (often written LORD in English Bibles), meaning “I AM.” Other titles include Elohim (God), Adonai (Lord), El Shaddai (God Almighty) and Abba (Father).
entries.explanation: Each name highlights part of God’s character. “Jehovah” is an older English form of Yahweh. Many names are combined with descriptions, such as Yahweh Jireh, “the LORD will provide” (Genesis 22:14). Jesus applied the “I AM” name to himself (John 8:58).

entries.question: Do Christians, Jews and Muslims worship the same God?
also_asked: Is Allah the same as the Christian God?
entries.short_answer: All three faiths claim to worship the God of Abraham, but they describe him very differently. Christians believe God is truly known only through Jesus Christ, whom Judaism and Islam do not accept as God the Son.
entries.explanation: Christianity shares the Hebrew Scriptures with Judaism and honours the God of Israel. But the New Testament teaches that rejecting the Son means not having the Father (1 John 2:23). Islam explicitly denies the Trinity and the death and deity of Jesus. Christians can respect people of other faiths while holding that Jesus is the only way to the Father.

entries.question: How can I know God personally?
also_asked: How do I have a relationship with God?
entries.short_answer: You can know God personally by turning from sin and trusting in Jesus Christ, who came to bring us to God. Then you grow in that relationship through prayer, the Bible and the church.
entries.explanation: Jesus defined eternal life as knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he sent (John 17:3). Sin separates us from God, but Christ died “to bring us to God” (1 Peter 3:18). See Theme 3 for how to be saved.

entries.question: Who is Jesus?
also_asked: Who was Jesus Christ?
What do Christians believe about Jesus?
entries.short_answer: Jesus is the eternal Son of God who became a man, lived a sinless life, died on the cross for our sins, rose from the dead and now reigns as Lord. He is the only Saviour and the centre of the Christian faith.
entries.explanation: Jesus was born in Bethlehem, grew up in Nazareth and taught in Israel in the first century. Christians believe he was far more than a teacher: he is “the Word” who was with God and was God, and who “became flesh” (John 1:1, 14). The title “Christ” means “Anointed One” (Messiah), the promised King of Israel.

entries.question: Is Jesus God?
also_asked: Did Jesus ever claim to be God?
Is Jesus the Son of God?
entries.short_answer: Yes. The Bible teaches that Jesus is fully God, the second person of the Trinity. He claimed divine authority and accepted worship, and the apostles called him God.
entries.explanation: Jesus forgave sins (Mark 2:5–7), claimed the divine name “I AM” (John 8:58), said “I and the Father are one” (John 10:30) and accepted Thomas’ words “My Lord and my God!” (John 20:28). His opponents understood these as claims to deity (John 10:33). “Son of God” in his case means sharing God’s very nature, not being created.

entries.question: Was Jesus fully human?
also_asked: How can Jesus be both God and man?
Did Jesus have human feelings?
entries.short_answer: Yes. Jesus is fully God and fully man in one person. He had a real human body and mind, grew tired and hungry, wept and suffered, yet never sinned.
entries.explanation: The church has summarised this as one person with two natures, divine and human, without mixing or separating them (the Council of Chalcedon, AD 451). Because he is human, Jesus could represent us and die in our place; because he is God, his sacrifice has infinite worth.

entries.question: Did Jesus really exist?
also_asked: Is there evidence Jesus was a real person?
Is Jesus a myth?
entries.short_answer: Yes. Almost all historians, Christian and non-Christian, agree that Jesus of Nazareth was a real first-century Jewish teacher who was crucified under Pontius Pilate.
entries.explanation: Besides the New Testament, which contains early sources written within decades of his life, Jesus is mentioned by the Jewish historian Josephus (around AD 93) and the Roman historian Tacitus (around AD 116), who records his execution under Pilate. The rapid growth of the church in Jerusalem also needs a historical explanation.

entries.question: What is the virgin birth and why does it matter?
also_asked: Was Mary a virgin?
Why was Jesus born of a virgin?
entries.short_answer: The virgin birth means Jesus was conceived by the Holy Spirit in the womb of Mary without a human father. It shows that he is uniquely God’s Son and that salvation comes from God, not human effort.
entries.explanation: Matthew and Luke both record it, and Matthew links it to Isaiah 7:14. It marks the moment the eternal Son took on human nature (the incarnation). Evangelicals hold it as an essential teaching about who Jesus is.

entries.question: Why did Jesus have to die?
also_asked: Why did Jesus die on the cross?
Couldn’t God just forgive us?
entries.short_answer: Jesus died to pay the penalty for our sins so that we could be forgiven and reconciled to God. Because God is just, sin had to be dealt with; because God is loving, he dealt with it himself in his Son.
entries.explanation: The Bible says “the wages of sin is death” (Romans 6:23). Jesus, who had no sin, took our place as a substitute and bore our sin (Isaiah 53:5–6; 2 Corinthians 5:21). This is often called substitutionary atonement. His death also defeated the powers of evil and showed God’s love.

entries.question: Did Jesus really rise from the dead?
also_asked: Is the resurrection true?
What is the evidence for the resurrection?
entries.short_answer: Yes. Christians believe Jesus rose bodily from the grave on the third day. This is the foundation of the faith: without it, Paul says, our faith is useless.
entries.explanation: Key facts widely accepted by historians include: Jesus died by crucifixion; his tomb was found empty; many people, including sceptics like James and Paul, believed they saw him alive; and the disciples were transformed and willing to suffer for this claim. One of the earliest records, 1 Corinthians 15:3–8, lists eyewitnesses, including over 500 people at once.

also_asked: Did Jesus go to hell?

entries.short_answer: Jesus told the repentant thief, “Today you will be with me in Paradise” (Luke 23:43). Beyond that, Christians interpret a few difficult passages differently.

entries.question: Why is Jesus called the Son of Man?

entries.short_answer: “Son of Man” was Jesus’ favourite title for himself. It points to his true humanity and, especially, to the divine figure in Daniel 7 who receives an everlasting kingdom from God.
entries.explanation: In Daniel 7:13–14, “one like a son of man” comes on the clouds and is given dominion and worship. At his trial, Jesus applied this to himself (Mark 14:62), and the high priest called it blasphemy.

entries.question: Is Jesus the Messiah promised in the Old Testament?
also_asked: What prophecies did Jesus fulfil?
entries.short_answer: Yes. Christians believe Jesus fulfilled the Old Testament promises of a coming Saviour-King, including his descent from David, birth in Bethlehem, suffering and death for sin, and resurrection.
entries.explanation: Examples include Micah 5:2 (born in Bethlehem), Isaiah 53 (the suffering servant who bears sin), Psalm 22 (details of crucifixion) and Zechariah 9:9 (entering Jerusalem on a donkey). After his resurrection Jesus explained how all the Scriptures pointed to him (Luke 24:27, 44).

entries.question: Was Jesus just a good teacher or prophet?
also_asked: Was Jesus only a moral teacher?
Do Muslims believe in Jesus?
entries.short_answer: Jesus’ own claims rule out that option. He claimed to be God, to forgive sins and to be the only way to the Father. A mere good teacher would not say such things.
entries.explanation: C. S. Lewis famously argued that someone making Jesus’ claims is either deluded, deceiving, or truly Lord. Islam honours Jesus as a prophet but denies his deity and crucifixion, which Christians see as contradicting the eyewitness record.

entries.question: What did Jesus teach?
also_asked: What was Jesus’ main message?
entries.short_answer: Jesus’ central message was the coming of the kingdom of God and the call to repent and believe the good news. He taught love for God and neighbour, humility, forgiveness, and faith in himself as the way to eternal life.
entries.explanation: Key teaching includes the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5–7), many parables, and his summary of the law: love God with all your heart and love your neighbour as yourself (Matthew 22:37–40). He also taught plainly about his coming death and resurrection.

entries.question: Why did Jesus teach in parables?
also_asked: What is a parable?
entries.short_answer: A parable is a short story from everyday life that teaches a spiritual truth. Jesus used them to reveal truth to those willing to listen while hiding it from those who had hardened their hearts.
entries.explanation: Jesus explained this himself in Matthew 13:10–17. Famous parables include the Prodigal Son, the Good Samaritan and the Sower. Each usually has one or a few main points rather than a hidden meaning in every detail.

entries.question: What miracles did Jesus perform, and why?
also_asked: Did Jesus really do miracles?
entries.short_answer: Jesus healed the sick, cast out demons, calmed storms, fed thousands and raised the dead. His miracles showed his compassion and proved his authority as the Son of God.
entries.explanation: John calls them “signs” because they point to who Jesus is (John 20:30–31). Even his opponents did not deny that he did remarkable works; they attributed them to other sources (Mark 3:22).

entries.question: Will Jesus come back?

entries.short_answer: Christians are called to respect and obey governing authorities, pay taxes and pray for leaders, because God established government for order and justice. But when the government commands what God forbids, or forbids what God commands, Christians must obey God.
entries.explanation: Romans 13:1–7 and 1 Peter 2:13–17 teach submission to authorities. When ordered to stop preaching about Jesus, the apostles replied, “We must obey God rather than men” (Acts 5:29). Christians may participate in public life in many ways, holding different political views, while their ultimate loyalty is to Christ’s kingdom.

glossary.meaning: Hebrew for “truly” or “so be it”; said to agree with a prayer or truth. Jesus often began teaching with “Truly (Amen) I tell you.”
Extra books in Catholic and Orthodox Bibles, not accepted as Scripture by Protestants.
“One who is sent.” The Twelve chosen by Jesus, plus Paul, commissioned as eyewitnesses of the risen Christ to lay the church’s foundation.
A view (after Jacobus Arminius, 1560–1609) that God’s choice of who is saved rests on his foreknowledge of faith, and that people can resist God’s grace.
How God makes sinners “at one” with him through Christ’s death paying for sin.
Receiving new spiritual life from the Holy Spirit.
A view (after John Calvin, 1509–1564) that God chose specific people for salvation by grace alone and his grace effectively brings them to faith.
The list of books recognised as inspired Scripture: 66 books in Protestant Bibles.
The meal of bread and cup by which Christians remember Jesus’ death until he returns.
The view that men and women are equal in worth but given some different roles, with the office of pastor or elder reserved for qualified men.
A binding, solemn relationship God makes with people, with promises and commitments. Key covenants in Scripture are with Noah, Abraham, Moses (at Sinai), David, and the New Covenant in Christ.
A way of reading the Bible that sees it unified by God’s covenants, with the church as the continuation of God’s one people.
A follower and learner of Jesus who trusts him and seeks to obey him.

A way of reading the Bible (developed in the 1800s, linked to John Nelson Darby) that divides history into periods and keeps a distinction between Israel and the church; it usually holds a pre-tribulation rapture.
The view that all church and family leadership roles are open equally to men and women.
A church leader who teaches and shepherds the congregation.
The study of “last things”: Christ’s return, judgment, heaven and the new creation.
From the Greek word for “good news.” Protestant Christians who stress the Bible’s authority, the cross of Christ, personal conversion and sharing the gospel.
Trusting in Jesus Christ for forgiveness and eternal life.
Any person who is not Jewish. The gospel is for Jews and Gentiles alike.
The good news that Jesus died for our sins and rose again, so all who trust him are forgiven.
God’s undeserved kindness and favour toward sinners.
Hebrew for “Praise Yah” (praise the LORD).
The eternal Son of God taking on full human nature as Jesus, without ceasing to be God.
God declaring a sinner righteous because of Christ, received by faith.
One who stands between two parties to bring them together. Jesus is the one mediator between God and people.
Hebrew “Mashiach” and Greek “Christos,” both meaning “Anointed One”: the promised Saviour-King. “Christ” is a title, not Jesus’ surname.
God’s promise to forgive sin and write his law on hearts, fulfilled through Jesus’ death.
A strict Jewish religious group in Jesus’ day, devoted to the law and their traditions. Jesus challenged many of them for hypocrisy, though some, like Nicodemus and Paul, came to faith.
Christ’s sacrifice satisfying God’s just anger against sin.
Being set free by the payment of a price. Christ redeemed believers from sin through his blood.
A change of heart and mind that turns from sin to God.
Being raised bodily from the dead to new life. Jesus rose first; believers will be raised when he returns.
A practice Christ commanded the church to observe as a sign of the gospel. Protestants recognise two: baptism and the Lord’s Supper. Some prefer the word “ordinance.”
Being rescued by God from sin and its penalty and brought into eternal life with him.
The lifelong process of becoming more like Christ through the Holy Spirit.
Any failure to love and obey God in thought, word, deed or attitude.
God’s rule and control over all things.
One God existing eternally as Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
